### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dc3879499d10a08b00bb9d412f5f25af482825f9` — the merge of head `340dfe9dcc873fe8f07f05f92231826bb8b3525a` into base `86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dc3879499d10a08b00bb9d412f5f25af482825f9 && git checkout dc3879499d10a08b00bb9d412f5f25af482825f9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34 340dfe9dcc873fe8f07f05f92231826bb8b3525a && git checkout -B drift-repro 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34 && git merge --no-ff 340dfe9dcc873fe8f07f05f92231826bb8b3525a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `340dfe9dcc873fe8f07f05f92231826bb8b3525a`
Local-runs: none

PR #22602 for card #22577, segment 3 of ruling A on #22438 (director record 6079645593, the maintainer's 「A + 扫类」; split request 6092059305). Inputs read: the card body and both comments (claim 6093168292, os-dev-report 6093472682), the two ruling comments, the PR body, its 3-file list, the net diff against `main` at the base `86f53a4b8d`, the base-sha text of `auth-gate.ts` and `anonymous-deny.ts` that the diff edits or cites, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The allow-list widens by exactly one exact route — right.** The diff adds `['approvals', 'act']` to the module-private `ALLOW_ROUTES`. On the base matcher (`matchesAllowlistedRoute`, read at `86f53a4b8d`) an entry matches only when the segments after the mount base and one optional scope are the route and end there. So the paths whose answer moves are: `/approvals/act`, `/api/approvals/act`, `/api/v1/approvals/act`, each unscoped or under one `/environments/{id}` or `/projects/{id}` scope immediately after the base, with query, trailing slashes and empty segments stripped as for every existing entry. No prefix rule, no wildcard, no second approvals path. `/approvals/act/x`, `/approvals/actx`, `/api/v1/approvals/requests/…`, `/data/approvals/act`, `/api/v2/approvals/act`, case and percent-encoded variants all stay gated. That is the card's「exact path only」and the ruling's item 1 for `packages/core`.
2. **`evaluateAuthGate` passes a held session on the act route and holds it next door — right.** This is the one live reader effect: the dispatcher's `enforceAuthGate`. REST `enforceAuth` never sees the path (no REST route serves it). The gate is method-agnostic, like every entry; no handler exists for a method other than `GET`/`POST` on either mount, so nothing wider is reached.
3. **`shouldDenyAnonymous` stops denying an anonymous request that names the act route — right.** `anonymous-deny.ts` (base) defers its control-plane exemption to `isAuthGateAllowlisted` for a non-empty path. ADR-0043 serves this page to a bearer with no session at all, so the exemption is the designed answer whether or not a shipped seam passes a path (the dev measured none; that reachability claim is the dev's and does not change the judgment).
4. **The environment-scoped spellings are admitted — right, not a loosening.** Judged in ③.
5. **Before segment 2 lands, a held session at the act route on the dispatcher gets `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` instead of the policy's `403` — right and harmless.** The ruling's own premise is that `http-dispatcher.ts` has no approvals domain; nothing is served, and anonymous callers already get that 404.
6. **Public surface — unchanged in shape.** No export is added, removed or renamed in `@objectstack/core`; the exported predicate's accept set grows by the route in point 1 and nothing else.
7. **Ruling scope held.** Only the `packages/core` segment is in the diff: no spec member, no dispatcher domain, no hono change, no plugin change (segments 1, 2, 4 untouched). The PR body states the boundary in one line, as the card requires. The `BOUNDARY` test's `preEntryAllowlisted` is a faithful transcription of the base matcher (same `MOUNT_BASES`, `SCOPE_SEGMENTS`, `auth` rule and exact-length route comparison), and its independently built expected set is the 63 paths of point 1 over the test vocabulary.
8. **Governed surfaces — none touched.** File list: `.changeset/…`, `packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.test.ts`. Head repo is the base repo (not a fork).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22577-approvals-act-allowlist.md`: `@objectstack/core` at `minor`. The diff publishes a behavioural widening of a released package: additive, nothing removed or renamed, no authorable key touched. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed; `patch` would be wrong for a widening; `skip-changeset` does not apply because the package publishes. `minor` matches what the diff publishes — right.
- `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body and in the changeset body, no arm written (allowed: at most one). The direction is a widening, so `(narrowing)` would have been wrong and `yes` with `minor` meets the floor. The claim comment's「Widening」reading agrees — right.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag (PR body §3, ⚠️ for the reviewer): the scoped spellings `/environments/{id}/approvals/act`, `/api/v1/environments/{id}/approvals/act`, `/api/v1/projects/{id}/approvals/act` are admitted.** Answered, not escalated. The scope normalisation is the gate's standing rule for every entry (`health`, `me/apps`, …): one scope, only immediately after the base, with an id; the dispatcher evaluates the gate before it strips the scope and then routes the same exact path to the same handler. The authentication on that handler is the single-use token, identical to the self-hosted raw-app mount. The route set is the gate's standard shape of one entry, not a wider rule, so the card's stop condition (wider than the self-hosted mount's authentication) is not met.
- **`open_questions`: `[]`** — nothing to answer.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`, three, read:**
  - the dispatcher membership gate (`enforceProjectMembership`) runs after this gate with no `/approvals` skip entry, so once segment 2 lands a signed-in non-member following a forwarded link would be refused before the token is read. Correctly outside this card (the ruling scopes it to the allow-list), real for segment 2. ⚠️ Its declared carrier is「segment 2's PR」, which does not exist yet; today it lives only in this PR's acceptance notes. The owning seat should relay it onto segment 2's card (or the parent #22438) so the runtime lane reads it before that domain lands. Not a defect of this diff.
  - the `AnonymousDenyInput.path` docstring parenthesis omits the new route (it already omitted `me/apps`) and defers to the predicate — cosmetic, carrier none, accepted.
  - the #7898 ratchet left verbatim — right: its corpus cannot reach `approvals/act`, so its transcription stays exact, and the new `BOUNDARY` test is this change's ratchet.
- **Deviations (os-dev-report):** the attribution-trailer form follows AGENTS.md; the throwaway dispatcher measurement was never committed and the 3-file list confirms it. Neither is a contract matter.
